coverage_argument.justification: Equal coefficients cannot work because distinct positive cubes differ by at least $7$. A common factor of the coefficients divides the difference. For $A<B$, any solution has $x/y$ reduced, since a common divisor of $x,y$ has its cube dividing $1$. It also has $x≥ y$: if $x<y$ then $By^3-Ax^3≥ y^3-x^3>1$. Put $t=x/y$ and $u=(B/A)^{1/3}>1$. Factoring the difference of cubes gives $|t-u|=1/[Ay^3(t^2+tu+u^2)]<1/(3y^3)$. For $Q=16H^2$ and $z=⌊ Qu⌋$, the rational $z/Q$ is within $1/Q$ of $u$. Thus $|t-z/Q|<(1/3+1/16)/y^2<1/(2y^2)$ whenever $y≤ H$. By Legendre’s continued fraction criterion, the reduced fraction $t$ is a convergent of $z/Q$, including the case of equality $t=z/Q$. The Euclidean algorithm enumerates these convergents exactly with nondecreasing positive denominators. Substitution checks both signs, and swapping the two coefficients just swaps the multipliers and reverses the sign.
